We follow standard USA Pickleball rally scoring option rules (Section 14.A) with the
following clarifications/modifications:

score: the player on the right (baseline facing the net) serves if the score is even, and
the player on the left serves if the score is odd.
• Switching Sides: Players only switch sides after winning a point on their own serve.
The same player continues serving from the new side.
• Side Outs & Scoring: If the serving team loses a rally, a side out occurs; the
opposing team earns a point and takes over the serve.

receiving except for the winning point (see next item).

point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,

that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using

be serving to score the game-winning point.

best point differential of all games played. This tie-
breaker does not apply across multiple pools where

example, Team A wins their first match, 11-8, 11-4, so

Match Score Sheet
Once both teams complete Match Setup, print the Match Score Sheet to view match details,
player names, and the format of play. You are able to print this if both teams have not
completed their Match Setup but those teams not completed will be blank.
• Button Color: Stays red until both teams enter their lineups, turning green once
both setups are complete.
• Printing: Print the sheet only after the button turns green. Printing early will leave

player or doubles team withdraws, retires, or is
forfeited from a round robin event, then that player’s
or team’s match results will not count toward the
standings of that event and the player or team will not
be eligible to participate in any elimination playoff or

rows.content:

seeded singles players or doubles teams play a single-elimination
or double-elimination playoff, using a match format of two of three
games to 11 points, one game to 15 points, or one game to 21
points, all win by two points.

rows.content:

Player Brackets) Single Elimination Without Consolation. The first

point margin wins. The final two players/teams in the winner’s
bracket play for the gold/first place and silver/second-place
medals. The determination of the final standings of the remaining

rows.content:
15.B.4.f Fifth Tie-Breaker. The fifth tie-breaker is the highest
number of points scored across all matches in the
round robin. This tie-breaker does not apply across
multiple pools where the number of teams in each
pool is not equal.

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Third Tie-Breaker
rows.content:
15.B.4.d Third Tie-Breaker. The third tie-breaker is the best
point differential of head-to-head games.

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Fourth Tie-Breaker
rows.content:
15.B.4.e Fourth Tie-Breaker. The fourth tie-breaker is the best
point differential of games played against the singles
player or doubles team with the next -highest number
of matches won. (For example, when players or teams
are tied for second-place, the total point differential
against the first-place singles player or doubles team is
used.)

1. CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
1.1. Club main website: https://lwrpickleballclub.com
1.2. League Management System (LMS) website: https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com
1.3. There are three seasons: Fall, Winter, and Spring.
1.4. Each season consists of a multi-week regular play followed by championships/playoƯs.
1.5. League teams are divided by Divisions based on DUPR ratings.
1.6. The Leagues consist of:
1.6.1. Weekday DUPR League – Gender doubles scheduled play during the week
1.6.2. Saturday League - Gender Doubles/Mixed play using the Picklebreaker™ format
(every other Saturday)
1.6.3. PrimeTime League – Gender doubles, aged 65+ scheduled play on Fridays

2. CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAINS
Each team in the League must be led by a designated Captain. That individual may also assume
the position of Co-Captain on a diƯerent team and can also serve as Captain for a team of the
opposite gender. However, an individual is not permitted to hold the role of Captain for more
than one team within the same gender category in a Division. A Captain or Co-Captain is not
required to be an active player on the team but may instead serve in a supportive capacity by
assisting with the responsibilities assigned to the Captain. For comprehensive “How to”
instructions for Captains, please consult the DUPR League Captains Guide.

4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

Rated) are eligible to participate in any division. However, it is strongly recommended that
a Certified DUPR Coach or qualified pickleball professional provide input to help
determine the player's most appropriate skill level. The team captain is ultimately
responsible for ensuring the player is placed in the proper division to promote balanced
and fair competition for all teams.

5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

5.6. DUPR Submission & Eligibility: All qualifying games will be automatically entered into
the DUPR rating system. Games that are forfeited, incomplete, or deemed ineligible will
not be recorded in DUPR (unless otherwise specified by a rule). Individuals/Players are
not authorized to independently submit any Club League scheduled games to DUPR.

5.7. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.7.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.7.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.7.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.

6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

6.1.4. Scoring: Each win earns 1 point with 9 total possible match points per date.

6.1.8. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both teams
are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the

6.1.9. Men’s/Women’s 9.1 Division: These divisions will initially be scheduled as a “flex

6.1.9.3. Scoring: Each win earns 1 point (5 total possible match points per date). If

The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are

camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

Rally Scoring Rules
We follow standard USA Pickleball rally scoring option rules (Section 14.A) with the
following clarifications/modifications:
• Service Positioning: After a side out, the first serve is determined by the team's
score: the player on the right (baseline facing the net) serves if the score is even, and

The scoring freeze starts when a team reaches one point below the game-winning score. From that point, that team can score the game-winning point only while serving.

Example: in a game to 25, a team freezes at 24. That team cannot win the final point unless it is serving. The other team may continue normal rally scoring until it also reaches its freeze point.

For win-by-two games: if the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, both teams become unfrozen and normal rally scoring resumes. After that, a team freezes again whenever its next point would win the game by two. If the score ties again, both teams unfreeze again. This continues until one team wins by two, and the game-winning point must always be scored while serving.

1.2. League Management System (LMS) website: https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com
1.3. There are three seasons: Fall, Winter, and Spring.
1.4. Each season consists of a multi-week regular play followed by championships/playoƯs.
1.5. League teams are divided by Divisions based on DUPR ratings.
1.6. The Leagues consist of:
1.6.1. Weekday DUPR League – Gender doubles scheduled play during the week
1.6.2. Saturday League - Gender Doubles/Mixed play using the Picklebreaker™ format
(every other Saturday)
1.6.3. PrimeTime League – Gender doubles, aged 65+ scheduled play on Fridays

2. CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAINS
Each team in the League must be led by a designated Captain. That individual may also assume
the position of Co-Captain on a diƯerent team and can also serve as Captain for a team of the
opposite gender. However, an individual is not permitted to hold the role of Captain for more
than one team within the same gender category in a Division. A Captain or Co-Captain is not
required to be an active player on the team but may instead serve in a supportive capacity by
assisting with the responsibilities assigned to the Captain. For comprehensive “How to”
instructions for Captains, please consult the DUPR League Captains Guide.

4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

Rated) are eligible to participate in any division. However, it is strongly recommended that
a Certified DUPR Coach or qualified pickleball professional provide input to help
determine the player's most appropriate skill level. The team captain is ultimately
responsible for ensuring the player is placed in the proper division to promote balanced
and fair competition for all teams.

5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

5.6. DUPR Submission & Eligibility: All qualifying games will be automatically entered into
the DUPR rating system. Games that are forfeited, incomplete, or deemed ineligible will
not be recorded in DUPR (unless otherwise specified by a rule). Individuals/Players are
not authorized to independently submit any Club League scheduled games to DUPR.

5.7. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.7.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.7.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.7.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.
